name: Prehistoric Thames
blurb: A wide, braided tidal river between gravel terraces and marsh. Woodland is cleared gradually from the Bronze Age. No town stands here; evidence for settlement on the site of the later City is slight.

name: Roman Londinium
blurb: A new town founded around 47–50 CE beside a bridge. Burned in 60/61, rebuilt with a forum, amphitheatre, fort and quays, walled around 200, then shrinking through the 3rd and 4th centuries.

name: Post-Roman & Anglo-Saxon
blurb: The walled city is largely empty for generations. A trading settlement, Lundenwic, grows to the west along the Strand; from 886 settlement moves back inside the Roman walls.

name: Norman & Medieval London
blurb: The Tower, a vast cathedral, a stone bridge lined with houses, over a hundred parish churches and many religious houses. Westminster grows as a separate royal centre.

name: Tudor London
blurb: Rapid growth beyond the walls. The monasteries are dissolved and converted, St Paul's loses its spire (1561), the Royal Exchange opens and playhouses rise on Bankside.

name: Jacobean London
blurb: The city of James I: a crowded timber metropolis of roughly 200,000 or more, with the first strict classical building, the Banqueting House (1619–22), at Whitehall.
